key_insight: LLM browser agents often completed sequencing prior authorization tasks but rarely withheld deficient cases for the correct reason, suggesting a bias toward submission.
clinical_relevance: Automating exome and genome sequencing prior authorization could reduce administrative burden, but unreliable withholding may undermine appropriate review.
method: Built a simulated payer portal and synthetic EHR containing 836 compliant and deliberately deficient patient profiles.
Evaluated three browser agents on task completion, form accuracy, and appropriate withholding.
Repeated evaluations twice on 100 profiles to assess run-to-run variability.
evidence_signal: Initial task completion ranged from 56.1% to 95.5%, while correct withholding ranged from 0% to 17.3%; only 18.0–48.0% of tasks had identical outcomes across three runs.
watch_item: These synthetic sandbox findings do not establish real-world clinical reliability; deployment would require further validation and human supervision.
paper_title: Hard to Halt: Automation Bias in Agent-Driven Sequencing Prior Authorization Workflows
